chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Jordan disbands the big band; re-recording his hits and The Milton Berle Show
summary: Told Jordan netted only five cents on the dollar, the band records 18 to 20 sides and appears on TV before breaking up in December.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: which we toured quite extensively. And I stayed with Louis' band right up until December... Well, actually, in the latter part of December, Louis Jordan decided to disband the band, to break the band up. From what I understood, I was told at that particular time that he had made so much money til he was actually only getting about 5 cents out of every dollar he made! So he decided to break the band up.

But before that, we did a thing of recording for... I don't remember the record company we did it for. I think it was Decca. But we recorded for about a week, which included about, I guess, at least 18 or 20 sides, if I can remember, of just about everything that he'd ever done. He re-recorded a lot of the things. And while we were in New York, I think, we also did The Milton Berle Show, which was a very big show on television. So it wound up being a very successful thing.
